statusDetail: Coverage-complete representative audit of homepage, city forecast, editorial listing, article, search journey, and 404 recovery. Excluded: account/commerce (not present), every city URL (Ajaccio represents the shared forecast template), specialist marine/mountain/beach templates, and destructive or authenticated flows.

page.framework: Drupal-rendered MPA with client-side forecast/map widgets
page.notes: Public French national weather and editorial service. Core HTML is server rendered; interactive maps, forecast states, advertising, and search hydrate client-side.

findings.summary: The site does not honor the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots under light and prefers-color-scheme: dark are pixel-identical, and the computed root colorScheme is “normal”.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven surface, text, icon, and browser-chrome colors using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Animations continue when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe confirmed the media query matched while five animations remained running, including four 600ms animations and one 2000ms animation.
findings.suggestedFix: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, remove non-essential transitions and auto-motion or reduce them to near-instant state changes.

findings.summary: The interface does not adapt to increased contrast, and existing text contrast failures remain.
findings.evidence: The prefers-contrast: more screenshot is visually unchanged; axe found 23 color-contrast failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast treatments and fix the underlying WCAG contrast failures without suppressing system colors.

findings.summary: Forecast state and document changes use abrupt swaps rather than View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The rendered stylesheet probe found no view-transition rules or names across forecast tabs/routes.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance forecast-tab and cross-document changes with View Transitions while preserving instant fallback behavior.

findings.summary: Long pages do not expose scroll progress or scroll-state-aware chrome.
findings.evidence: The homepage is 7,911 CSS pixels tall on mobile, while CSS inspection found no scroll-state or timeline feature and the captured header remains static.
findings.suggestedFix: Use lightweight scroll-state affordances such as a shrinking sticky header or progress marker, with reduced-motion support.

findings.summary: Menus and overlay surfaces are manually positioned rather than anchored declaratively.
findings.evidence: The DOM contains multiple custom modal/popup containers, while the feature probe found no anchor-name, position-anchor, or position-try usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Use popover plus CSS anchor positioning and position-try fallbacks for transient menus and attached overlays.

findings.summary: Overlay UI is implemented as custom div structures rather than semantic dialog/popover primitives.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found repeated .mf_modal and .modal_overlay divs, zero dialog, popover, or details primitives, and axe found focusable content inside aria-hidden UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace custom modal shells with dialog for modal tasks and popover for transient UI, relying on platform focus, top-layer, Escape, and light-dismiss behavior.

findings.summary: Mobile homepage chrome overlaps and competes with content near the bottom of the first viewport.
findings.evidence: The 360x800 screenshot shows a crowded, partially overlapping bottom carousel/navigation strip with clipped labels over editorial content.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or defer non-essential sticky/carousel chrome, reserve its space, and keep one clear content hierarchy at narrow widths.

findings.summary: Reusable components rely on viewport styling rather than container-level adaptation.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no @container rules or container-type declarations across the rendered homepage styles.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt container queries for reused cards, forecast panels, and navigation modules so they respond to their actual available width.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated on important controls.
findings.evidence: The focus probe reported outline-style none and no box-shadow for the search input, submit button, menu button, and many navigation links; axe also found non-focusable scroll regions.
findings.suggestedFix: Add strong :focus-visible styling, make scrollable regions keyboard focusable, and preserve at least 44x44 CSS-pixel targets.

findings.summary: The primary forecast page loads far outside good Core Web Vitals ranges.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 24.0s, CLS 0.592, FCP 6.6s and TBT 400ms (performance score 24); the independent trace measured LCP 10.02s.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP dependency chain, prioritize the LCP asset, reduce server/document latency and render-blocking work, and verify LCP below 2.5s and CLS below 0.1.

findings.summary: Late content causes severe layout movement on the forecast templates.
findings.evidence: The layout primitive measured CLS 0.465 on the mobile homepage and 0.658 on the Ajaccio page; 60 of 64 images lack explicit dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image, map, advertising, and async-module space with width/height or aspect-ratio and avoid injecting unreserved content above existing content.

findings.summary: Critical delivery is heavy and render-blocked.
findings.evidence: The HAR records 2.98 MB across 72 requests, four parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets, an uncompressed 716 KB first-party script, and 234 KB uncompressed HTML.
findings.suggestedFix: Compress text responses, reduce and inline only truly critical CSS, defer non-critical resources, split the monolithic script, and set useful cache headers.

findings.summary: Large amounts of shipped JavaScript and CSS are unused on the initial forecast view.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 735,048 bytes of unused JavaScript and 158,107 bytes of unused CSS; third parties transfer another 968,584 bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Split code by route/component, remove duplicate and legacy code, conditionally load maps/ads/editorial features, and enforce JavaScript/CSS budgets.

findings.summary: Controls and visual content have missing or invalid accessible names and roles.
findings.evidence: axe found critical missing alt text and unnamed select failures, serious unnamed links and prohibited ARIA, plus aria-hidden focusable content.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every control and meaningful image an accessible name, correct invalid roles/ARIA, and remove hidden descendants from the focus order.

findings.summary: Text contrast fails WCAG AA in repeated editorial content.
findings.evidence: axe found 23 color-contrast failure nodes, including dates and article-card copy.
findings.suggestedFix: Update text and surface tokens to achieve at least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text and essential UI.

findings.summary: Landmarks, focus handling, and keyboard access are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: axe found nested banner/contentinfo/complementary landmarks, two keyboard-inaccessible scrollable regions, and focusable elements inside aria-hidden #sidebar_page; the direct focus probe found invisible focus on key controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Use top-level landmarks, remove hidden UI from the focus order, make carousels/scroll regions keyboard operable, and provide a logical visible focus sequence.

findings.summary: The viewport configuration disables user zoom.
findings.evidence: axe’s critical meta-viewport rule failed because the viewport prevents text scaling/zooming.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale and user-scalable=no restrictions; retain width=device-width and initial-scale=1 so users can zoom and reflow.

findings.summary: The production page emits console errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s errors-in-console audit failed on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve runtime/network exceptions and add production monitoring that treats uncaught errors as release regressions.

findings.summary: Image asset sizing is unsound despite a valid doctype and UTF-8 charset.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 60 of 64 images without dimensions, five oversized images, three legacy-format images, and three missing alt values.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic dimensions, responsive srcset/sizes, and appropriately sized modern assets while retaining valid document metadata.

findings.summary: The page ships broken inspection metadata and browser issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed valid-source-maps and inspector-issues audits.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish matching production source maps to authorized tooling or omit broken references, and clear reported inspector/deprecation issues.

findings.summary: Some links are not crawlable and mobile friendliness is weakened by disabled zoom.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed crawlable-anchors; axe and Lighthouse also failed the meta-viewport zoom audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real descriptive href values for every navigational link and allow user scaling in the viewport metadata.

findings.summary: Rich pages do not expose structured data or social-preview metadata.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found zero JSON-LD blocks and zero Open Graph tags even though the site contains organization, forecast/place, and article entities.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate JSON-LD and Open Graph/Twitter metadata that matches visible Organization, Article, Place, and weather content.

findings.summary: HTTPS is used, but baseline security headers and cookie protections are missing.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy; didomi_token lacks Secure and mfsession uses SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, HSTS, nosniff, clickjacking defense, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; mark all HTTPS cookies Secure and use the strictest workable SameSite.

findings.summary: The default page load has a large tracking and advertising footprint.
findings.evidence: The tracker primitive found eight third-party origins including Google Tag Manager and DoubleClick; the HAR attributes 33 requests and 968,584 bytes to third parties.
findings.suggestedFix: Load non-essential analytics/advertising only after valid consent, minimize vendors and event volume, batch telemetry, and document retention and purposes.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: No HSTS, frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or CSP was returned for the main document.
findings.suggestedFix: Set HSTS, CSP with frame-ancestors and Trusted Types where feasible, strict referrer handling, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Custom hidden/runtime UI has inconsistent visibility and focus state.
findings.evidence: The DOM reports multiple custom modal shells as geometrically visible while axe finds aria-hidden focusable content; the mobile screenshot shows overlapping carousel chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Move transient UI to dialog/popover top-layer primitives, synchronize hidden/inert/focus state, and test narrow-edge positioning and async open/close cycles.

findings.summary: The French language is declared correctly, but layout CSS is not writing-mode resilient.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found html lang=fr and dir=ltr, but no logical-property usage and 450 physical left/right declarations in rendered CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Migrate layout spacing, sizing, and positioning to logical properties and test translated and RTL expansion even if French remains the primary locale.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bytes and creates layout risk.
findings.evidence: Of 64 images, 60 lack dimensions, 39 below-fold images are not lazy-loaded, five are oversized, 12 lack srcset, and three use legacy formats.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate right-sized AVIF/WebP variants with srcset/sizes, lazy-load below-fold images, and include intrinsic dimensions.

findings.summary: Non-essential third-party work consumes substantial resources during initial load.
findings.evidence: Eight third-party origins load on entry; ads, consent, analytics, and wrappers account for 33 requests and 968,584 transferred bytes before user interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-essential vendors until consent and intent, remove low-value wrappers, and budget third-party CPU/network cost.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts and media are disproportionate to the immediate forecast task.
findings.evidence: Third parties account for roughly one third of the 2.98 MB load, while the homepage also fetches editorial/video-related resources before they enter the viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load ads, video embeds, and editorial media near interaction/viewport; set per-template third-party and media budgets.

findings.summary: Forecast capability is crawler-visible but not exposed as a safe structured agent action.
findings.evidence: Raw HTML coverage is 85% on the homepage and 100% on the article, but the capability probe found no WebMCP/agentic tool registration or structured action surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Treat this as an emerging opportunity: expose read-only location lookup and forecast retrieval as schema-described, permission-bounded agent tools.

findings.summary: Repeated forecast-tab interaction increases retained heap and node count.
findings.evidence: After ten today/tomorrow cycles, the summary grew from 44.7 MB/1,211,243 nodes to 48.0 MB/1,275,325 nodes (about +3.25 MB and +64k nodes). Separate fresh-browser baselines reduce confidence, so this requires retained-path confirmation.
findings.suggestedFix: Capture baseline/target/final snapshots in one session, identify retained paths, and clean up listeners, timers, nodes, and caches on forecast-state teardown.

findings.summary: The initial page has a large memory footprint for a forecast/content page.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary reports 1,211,243 nodes, 4,955,903 edges, 154,521 closures, and 44.7 MB self-size before extended interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce initial modules and DOM, virtualize or defer below-fold content, and conditionally initialize maps, ads, and editorial features.
